script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for May 7. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Your immune system is smart—once it defeats an enemy, it remembers.  Next time that enemy appears, it's destroyed before you even feel sick.  Vaccines hack this system, introducing harmless versions of threats so your body learns to fight them in advance.

Your immune system creates 'memory cells' after fighting infections. These cells remember specific enemies for years or decades. Vaccines trigger this memory creation without requiring you to suffer through the actual disease. Smallpox killed hundreds of millions.  In 1796, Edward Jenner showed that cowpox infection prevented smallpox.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Preparation beats reaction.  Vaccines prove that training before battle determines outcomes.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Immune Appreciation - Know Your Defenders.

Here's your activity: Consider which vaccinations you've had. Each one trained your immune system against a specific threat. Your body now has memory cells ready to fight enemies you've never actually encountered. Preparation is protection. This helps you appreciate your immune system's learning ability.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about training your immune system can be applied to immune appreciation - know your defenders. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
